title: BAIT BridgeLock Emergency Procedures
description: Emergency response procedures for the 3-of-5 multisig bridge

pauseUnpause.description: Pause/unpause the BridgeLock contract to halt or resume all bridge operations

pause.trigger: Any confirmed security incident, suspicious activity, or operational emergency
pause.effect: All requestLockMint, confirmLockMint, initiateBurnRelease, confirmBurnRelease calls revert with 'Pausable: paused'
doesNotAffect: View functions (operators, isOperator, paused, getLockRequestCount, getBurnReleaseCount, dailyMinted)
Existing confirmed requests that have already been executed
WBAIT transfers (unless WBAIT is also paused separately)
procedure: 1. Owner calls pause() on BridgeLock contract
2. Optionally: Owner calls pause() on WBAIT contract (stops all wBAIT transfers)
3. Verify paused() returns true on BridgeLock
4. If WBAIT paused: Verify WBAIT.paused() returns true
5. Notify all 5 operators via emergency Signal group
6. Post incident to monitoring dashboard (#bridge-status channel)
7. Bridge monitor will auto-detect paused state and alert
8. Begin incident investigation (see incidentEscalationMatrix)
pause.safetyNote: Pausing is SAFE — no funds are at risk. Existing lock/burn state is preserved. Only new operations are blocked.

prerequisites: Root cause analysis complete and documented
Vulnerability patched (if applicable) and verified on testnet
External audit sign-off obtained (for P0/P1 security incidents)
All 5 operators notified and 3-of-5 explicitly agree to resume
Bridge monitor healthy and running for all operators
procedure: 1. Confirm ALL prerequisites are met — do not skip any
2. Owner calls unpause() on BridgeLock contract
3. If WBAIT was paused: Owner calls unpause() on WBAIT contract
4. Verify paused() returns false on BridgeLock
5. Monitor first 10 transactions closely for anomalies
6. Verify confirmLockMint and confirmBurnRelease work (test with small amount)
7. Resume normal monitoring intervals
8. Log unpause event with timestamp and authorization record
unpause.caution: Unpausing before root cause is resolved may re-expose the vulnerability. Always err on the side of caution.

operatorReplacement.description: Replace a compromised, lost, or unavailable operator key
operatorReplacement.trigger: Key compromise, HSM failure, operator departure, or extended unavailability (>72 hours)
operatorReplacement.timelock: 24 hours (TIMELOCK_DURATION in contract — cannot be bypassed)
operatorReplacement.whoCanPropose: Any existing operator or contract owner
operatorReplacement.whoCanConfirm: 3-of-5 existing operators (excluding the operator being replaced)
procedure: 1. Identify the operator index (0-4) to replace — use bridge monitor or cast call operators(i)
2. Generate new key in replacement operator's HSM (per key ceremony procedure in operator-onboarding.md §2)
3. Extract public key and Ethereum address from new HSM key
4. Verify new address is not zero, not duplicate, and valid checksum
5. Propose operator update on BridgeLock contract — this triggers the 24h timelock
6. Wait 24 hours for timelock to expire — this CANNOT be bypassed
7. During timelock: Other operators review replacement (verify new key, check ceremony compliance)
8. After timelock expires: Execute operator update with 3-of-5 confirmations from OTHER operators
9. The operator being replaced CANNOT confirm their own replacement
10. Verify on-chain: isOperator(newAddress) == true
11. Verify on-chain: isOperator(oldAddress) == false
12. Test new operator can call confirmLockMint or confirmBurnRelease
13. Decommission old HSM key: disable (CKA_ENABLED=false), do NOT delete — retain for audit trail
14. Update ceremony transcript with rotation record (old key, new key, timestamp, confirming operators)
15. Restart bridge monitoring with updated operator list
16. Notify all operators of completed replacement via encrypted channel

timelockPeriodBehavior.description: What happens during the 24-hour timelock period
timelockPeriodBehavior.bridgeOperations: Continue normally — existing operators can still confirm requests
timelockPeriodBehavior.newOperator: Cannot participate until timelock expires and update is executed
timelockPeriodBehavior.oldOperator: Can still confirm requests during timelock (key is still active)
timelockPeriodBehavior.cancellation: If replacement is deemed incorrect, proposal can be cancelled before timelock expires

emergencyAccelerated.description: When bridge is paused, operator replacement still requires 24h timelock
emergencyAccelerated.caveat: The timelock is a CONTRACT ENFORCED delay — it cannot be bypassed even by the owner
emergencyAccelerated.alternativeIfUrgent: If timelock must be bypassed: Deploy entirely new BridgeLock contract with new operator set and migrate state
emergencyAccelerated.migrationCost: New contract deployment + state migration + Etherscan verification + 48h monitoring
emergencyAccelerated.recommendation: Accept 24h downtime during emergency rotation; it's safer than emergency migration

quorumSafetyCheck.description: Ensure 3-of-5 threshold remains achievable during and after replacement
quorumSafetyCheck.duringReplacement: At least 3 of the remaining 4 operators must be available to confirm the replacement transaction
quorumSafetyCheck.afterReplacement: New operator must have functional HSM and be able to sign confirmations
quorumSafetyCheck.edgeCase_twoSimultaneous: If 2 operators are being replaced simultaneously, bridge operations halt until at least one replacement completes (only 3 operators remain, all must be available)
quorumSafetyCheck.edgeCase_threeUnavailable: If 3 operators are unavailable: Bridge cannot reach threshold — PAUSE and initiate emergency recovery (see disasterRecovery in hsm-configuration.json)

fundRecovery.description: Procedures for recovering or protecting bridge funds during emergencies
fundRecovery.conservationInvariant: totalSupply(wBAIT) == totalLockedOnL1(BAIT) — this must be maintained at all times

scenarios.cause: Operators unavailable, request invalid, or operators disagree on validity
scenarios.severity: LOW — no funds at risk on either chain
scenarios.impactOnL1: BAIT tokens remain locked on L1 — safe
scenarios.impactOnEthereum: No wBAIT minted until 3 confirmations — safe by design
recoveryOptions: Option A (Preferred): Contact missing operators via Signal/phone to confirm — usually resolves within hours
Option B: Replace unavailable operator (24h timelock) and have new operator confirm
Option C: If request is INVALID (wrong L1 tx, suspicious recipient): Leave unconfirmed — no wBAIT minted, L1 funds remain locked. Coordinate L1-side recovery if needed.
Option D: If ALL 5 operators agree request is invalid: No action needed — unconfirmed requests are harmless
scenarios.safetyProperty: wBAIT is ONLY minted AFTER 3 confirmations. Unconfirmed requests create no on-chain state change on Ethereum. L1 funds are locked but recoverable via L1 governance.
scenarios.timeToRecovery: Hours (if operators available) to 48h (if operator replacement needed)

scenarios.cause: Operators unavailable after user already burned wBAIT
scenarios.severity: HIGH — user's wBAIT is already burned; they need L1 release
scenarios.impactOnL1: BAIT tokens remain locked on L1 — awaiting operator confirmation to release
scenarios.userImpact: User has lost wBAIT on Ethereum and has not received BAIT on L1 — FUNDS IN LIMBO
recoveryOptions: Option A (URGENT): Contact missing operators to confirm L1 release — this is HIGH PRIORITY
Option B: Replace unavailable operator and have new operator confirm burn-release
Option C: Manual L1 release by remaining operators (off-chain coordination + on-chain confirmation)
Option D: If only 1-2 operators missing: 3 remaining operators can still confirm and execute
scenarios.safetyProperty: L1 tokens are still locked and safe — they can ONLY be released after 3 operator confirmations. The user WILL receive their BAIT once confirmations are obtained.
scenarios.timeToRecovery: Hours (if operators available) to 48h (if operator replacement needed)
scenarios.priority: HIGHEST — user funds are in limbo; treat as P1 incident

scenarios.cause: Bug in operator verification, malicious operator, or frontend error
scenarios.impact: wBAIT minted without corresponding L1 lock, or wrong amount minted
recoveryOptions: 1. PAUSE bridge immediately (both BridgeLock AND WBAIT)
2. Assess total incorrect mints — query all LockExecuted events and cross-reference with L1 locks
3. If small amount: Consider absorbing loss from treasury (if governance approves)
4. If large amount: Deploy corrected WBAIT with supply adjustment
5. Worst case: Full bridge migration — deploy new contracts, migrate valid state, blacklist invalid mints
6. External audit of how incorrect mint occurred
7. Update operator verification procedures to prevent recurrence
prevention: Each operator verifies independently on air-gapped workstation before signing
3-of-5 threshold means at least 3 operators must independently verify
Rate limit (100K wBAIT/day) caps maximum damage from any single exploit
Conservation invariant check in monitoring: totalSupply(wBAIT) should match total L1 locks
scenarios.timeToRecovery: 24-72 hours (depends on severity and migration complexity)

scenarios.cause: Sybil attacker creates many addresses, each hitting the 100K wBAIT/day limit
scenarios.severity: MEDIUM-HIGH — can mint large amounts across many addresses
scenarios.impact: Conservation invariant still holds per-address, but total bridge throughput exploited
recoveryOptions: 1. PAUSE bridge to stop further exploitation
2. Assess total minted across all Sybil addresses
3. Identify Sybil patterns (common funding source, similar timestamps, etc.)
4. If mints were valid (real L1 locks): No recovery needed — rate limit working as designed
5. If mints were invalid (no real L1 locks): Follow incorrect mint recovery procedure
6. Preventive: Consider per-operator rate limits, KYC whitelist, or delayed mint in next contract version
prevention: Monitor rate limit usage per recipient (bridge-monitoring.py does this automatically)
Alert when multiple addresses approach cap simultaneously (Sybil detection)
Track funding sources of new addresses (anomaly detection)
Rate limit of 100K wBAIT/day/address limits maximum per-address damage
scenarios.timeToRecovery: Hours (investigation) to days (if contract upgrade needed)

scenarios.cause: Legitimate bridge usage approaching maximum wBAIT supply
scenarios.severity: MEDIUM — bridge becomes unusable when cap is reached
scenarios.impact: New lock-mint requests will fail with 'WBAIT: exceeds max supply cap'
recoveryOptions: 1. Monitor SupplyCapApproaching events (emitted at 90% of cap = 18.9M wBAIT)
2. If legitimate usage: Consider governance proposal to increase cap (requires new WBAIT deployment)
3. Encourage burn-releases to reduce circulating supply
4. If approaching cap due to exploit: Pause and investigate
scenarios.prevention: Monitor totalSupply via bridge monitor; alert at 80% and 90% of cap

incidentEscalationMatrix.description: Escalation levels and response procedures for bridge incidents

levels.definition: Active exploit, funds at risk, or bridge security breach confirmed
examples: Unauthorized wBAIT mint detected (conservation invariant violated)
2+ operator keys compromised simultaneously
Smart contract vulnerability being actively exploited on mainnet
L1 bridge fund theft in progress
wBAIT minted without corresponding L1 lock
Bridge executing requests without proper 3-of-5 confirmation
automatedDetection: bridge-monitoring.py: Unexpected LockExecuted without 3 LockConfirmed events
bridge-monitoring.py: totalSupply(wBAIT) != expected total L1 locks
bridge-monitoring.py: OperatorUpdated event from unknown proposer
Prometheus alert: bait_bridge_lock_executed_total increases without corresponding confirmations

response.firstResponder: Any operator or automated monitoring system
actions: 1. PAUSE BridgeLock contract immediately (owner action)
2. PAUSE WBAIT contract immediately (owner action — stops all transfers)
3. Page all 5 operators + owner via PagerDuty/Signal emergency group
4. Assess scope of exploit: Check recent LockExecuted/BurnExecuted events for anomalies
5. Identify exploited addresses and amounts
6. If funds actively draining: Attempt emergency L1 lock (if applicable)
7. Engage external security auditor (CertiK/Halborn/Trail of Bits — have retainer)
8. Document timeline with precise timestamps (UTC)
9. Post incident to security channel with full details
10. Do NOT unpause until external audit confirms fix

communication.within1hour: External auditor + legal counsel (if funds lost > $10K)

levels.definition: Suspected compromise or operational emergency that could escalate to P0
examples: Single operator key compromise suspected (but not confirmed)
HSM cluster failure (operator cannot sign — but 3-of-5 still achievable)
Bridge monitor detects anomalous confirmation pattern (wrong operators confirming)
Rate limit being systematically approached by many addresses (Sybil pattern)
Unexpected operator replacement proposal submitted
Contract owner transfer initiated without authorization
automatedDetection: bridge-monitoring.py: Confirmation from operator not in operator list
bridge-monitoring.py: Multiple addresses hitting >80% rate limit simultaneously
bridge-monitoring.py: OperatorUpdated event without prior operator coordination
HSM audit: Failed authentication attempts on operator key

actions: 1. Notify all other operators via Signal emergency group
2. Assess whether to pause bridge (if risk of escalation to P0)
3. If key compromise: Disable HSM key immediately (CKA_ENABLED=false)
4. Begin operator key rotation procedure (see operatorReplacement)
5. If HSM failure: Initiate HSM failover/recovery (provider-specific)
6. Document incident with timestamps and evidence
7. If rate limit Sybil: Monitor closely; pause if threshold breached
8. Set monitoring to enhanced mode (15-second poll, all alerts to Signal)

levels.definition: Operational issue affecting bridge throughput but not security
examples: 1-2 operators unavailable (3-of-5 still achievable)
RPC endpoint degradation (slow event processing, missed blocks)
Bridge monitoring system gap (monitor down, false positive)
Single request stalled > 30 minutes without enough confirmations
HSM performance degradation (slow signing, >5s per operation)
Daily rate limit hit for a single address (legitimate usage)
automatedDetection: bridge-monitoring.py: RPC connection error or block lag > 60s

actions: 1. Investigate root cause
2. Contact unavailable operators via phone/Signal
3. If RPC issues: Switch to backup RPC endpoint (update RPC_URL in .env, restart monitor)
4. If operator unavailable >4h: Document and track; escalate to P1 if unavailable >24h
5. If monitoring gap: Restart bridge monitor; check state file for resume point
6. Resume normal operations once resolved

levels.definition: Minor issue or informational alert requiring eventual action
examples: Approaching rate limit for single address (near 80% daily cap)
Monitoring alert that resolves itself (transient RPC error)
Scheduled operator key rotation due in next 7 days
Minor monitoring dashboard display issue
HSM firmware update available (non-critical)
Bridge monitor log rotation needed
automatedDetection: Cron: Key rotation due in 7 days (check hsm-configuration.json schedule)

actions: 1. Acknowledge alert in monitoring system (don't let it nag)
2. Investigate if pattern persists (check last 7 days of alerts)
3. Schedule corrective action if needed (add to next sprint)
4. Update runbook if new scenario discovered
5. If rate limit alert: Verify recipient is legitimate; consider whitelist if recurring
response.communication: Log in incident tracker; notify coordinator if recurring pattern

escalationRules: P3 → P2: If issue persists > 24 hours OR affects multiple operators OR occurs >3 times in 7 days
P2 → P1: If security implications suspected OR operator unavailable > 24h OR bridge throughput degraded >50%
P1 → P0: If exploit confirmed OR funds at risk OR >= 2 operator keys compromised simultaneously
Any level → P0: If >= 2 operator keys compromised simultaneously (cannot guarantee 3-of-5 integrity)
P2 → P1: If single stalled burn-release > 4 hours (user funds in limbo)
Auto-escalate: Bridge monitor auto-escalates stalled requests from P2→P1 after 2×STALL_THRESHOLD_MIN
deEscalationRules: P0 → P1: After bridge is paused and funds secured; no active exploit
P1 → P2: After compromised key disabled and rotation initiated; no evidence of exploit
P2 → P3: After root cause identified and fix implemented; normal operations resumed
P1 → P0 is NOT allowed without new evidence (never de-escalate from confirmed exploit)

emergency.useFor: P0 and P1 incidents — immediate response required
emergency.setup: Create Signal group 'BAIT Bridge Emergency' — verify all members with safety numbers
emergency.backupChannel: Phone call tree if Signal unavailable

operational.useFor: P2 and P3 incidents — operational coordination
operational.setup: Create Telegram group 'BAIT Bridge Ops' — enable slow mode (30s) to prevent noise

public.setup: Configure Discord webhook in bridge-monitoring.py ALERT_WEBHOOK

audit.useFor: Post-incident review, audit reports, compliance documentation
audit.setup: Exchange PGP keys during onboarding; verify fingerprints via Signal

monitoring.useFor: Automated alerts from bridge monitor (stalled requests, rate limits, contract events)

flow: Each person confirms receipt and understanding of incident

automatedDetectionTriggers.description: Conditions that automatically trigger incident response

triggers.trigger: Bridge monitor detects LockExecuted without 3 preceding LockConfirmed events
triggers.action: Auto-alert to Signal group + pause request to owner

triggers.trigger: Bridge monitor detects contract paused state change
triggers.severity: P1 if paused by owner; P0 if paused by unknown
triggers.action: Auto-alert to Signal group with current state
Auto-alert to Signal group + reload operators

triggers.trigger: Request stalled > STALL_THRESHOLD_MIN minutes without reaching 3 confirmations
triggers.action: Alert to webhook + Signal (if >2× threshold, escalate to P1)

triggers.trigger: Rate limit usage > RATE_LIMIT_PCT% for any recipient
triggers.action: Alert to webhook; monitor for Sybil patterns

triggers.trigger: HSM signing operation fails or times out
triggers.action: Alert operator; check HSM health; failover if possible

triggers.trigger: Bridge monitor RPC connection lost for > 5 minutes
triggers.action: Exponential backoff + fallback RPC; alert if all RPCs fail
Alert all operators; prepare governance proposal for cap adjustment

recoveryVerification.description: Steps to verify bridge is healthy after recovery from an incident
postRecoveryChecklist: 2. Verify WBAIT.paused() == false (if WBAIT was also paused)
3. Verify all 5 operators are registered: isOperator(addr) == true for each
4. Verify operator count: No unexpected operators added or removed
5. Verify bridge monitor is running and healthy for all operators
6. Check recent events: No anomalous LockExecuted or BurnExecuted since unpause
7. Verify rate limits are functioning correctly
8. Test with a small lock-mint request (test amount) and confirm through 3-of-5
9. Verify wBAIT conservation invariant: totalSupply == expected total L1 locks
10. Check HSM audit logs for any unauthorized access during incident window
11. Verify bridge monitor Prometheus metrics are updating (bait_bridge_last_processed_block increasing)
12. Run bridge monitor in enhanced logging mode for 24 hours post-recovery

conservationInvariantCheck.description: Verify that totalSupply(wBAIT) matches total L1 locked amount
procedure: 1. Query WBAIT.totalSupply() on Ethereum
2. Query all LockExecuted events to sum total minted wBAIT
3. Query all BurnInitiated events to sum total burned wBAIT
4. Verify: totalSupply == totalMinted - totalBurned
5. If mismatch: This is a P0 incident — conservation invariant violated
6. Cross-reference with L1: Total L1 locked should match totalSupply(wBAIT)
conservationInvariantCheck.automatedCheck: Run daily via bridge-monitoring.py daily summary

postIncidentChecklist: 1. Verify bridge contract state is consistent (no corrupted state)
2. Run conservation invariant check: totalSupply(wBAIT) == total L1 locks
3. Check all recent lock requests: no unexpected mints since incident
4. Check all recent burn releases: no unexpected L1 releases since incident
5. Verify operator set is correct and all 5 are operational (can sign)
6. Review HSM audit logs for any unauthorized access attempts during incident
7. Run bridge monitor in enhanced logging mode for 24 hours post-incident
8. Write incident report (timeline, root cause, remediation, prevention measures)
9. Share incident report with all operators (PGP-encrypted email)
10. Share incident report with external auditor (PGP-encrypted email)
11. Update emergency procedures based on lessons learned (update this file)
12. Update operator onboarding guide if procedural changes needed
13. Schedule follow-up security review within 7 days (for P0) or 30 days (for P1)
14. Update monitoring thresholds or alerts if new scenario discovered
15. If incident was P0: Schedule external re-audit of bridge contracts
16. Archive all incident artifacts (logs, screenshots, transcripts) for 7 years
17. Verify all automated detection triggers are still functional after changes
18. Run DR test on staging to validate any procedural changes

preApprovedEmergencyActions.description: Actions that operators are pre-authorized to take without additional approval during emergencies
anyOperator: Request bridge pause (must contact owner who executes)
Disable their own HSM key (if they suspect their own key is compromised)
Alert all other operators via Signal emergency group
Initiate enhanced monitoring (15-second poll, all alerts to Signal)
ownerOnly: Execute unpause() on BridgeLock (only after incident resolution)
Execute unpause() on WBAIT (only after incident resolution)
requires3of5Approval: Any parameter change on BridgeLock contract
neverPreApproved: Delete HSM keys (disable only, never delete)
Modify bridge monitor configuration to suppress alerts
Deploy new contracts without external audit

contactRotationSchedule.description: On-call operator rotation for 24/7 bridge coverage
contactRotationSchedule.model: Follow-the-sun with 3 geographic zones ensuring >=3 operators always available
contactRotationSchedule.minimumAvailable: 3 operators at all times (to maintain 3-of-5 threshold)
contactRotationSchedule.escalationIfBelow3: P0 — bridge cannot confirm requests; all operators paged
contactRotationSchedule.handoverProtocol: Outgoing operator briefs incoming on any pending requests, active incidents, and anomalies
